Primary Contribution: Resolves the fundamental tradeoff between reconstruction and generative diffusability in high-compression latent spaces.

cards.title: Visual Tokenization Dilemma Overview
bullets: Dilemma: Higher reconstruction accuracy (lower rFID) leads to worse diffusion generation (higher gFID).
Solution: VFM Alignment (VA-VAE) establishes a strictly monotonic Pareto frontier.

slides.title: The Reconstruction vs. Generation Optimization Dilemma
slides.subtitle: Why Autoencoders with Superior Reconstruction Fail to Produce Quality Diffusion Generative Models

cards.title: Empirical Manifestation of the Dilemma
bullets: Counter-Intuitive Failure: Increasing VAE latent channels (e.g. from f16d16 to f16d64) improves reconstruction (rFID 0.49 → 0.18) but severely degrades generation (gFID 20.3 → 45.8).
Generative Collapse: High-dimensional visual latents scatter across unconstrained sub-manifolds, crippling score-matching training in Diffusion Transformers.

side_note.title: Relationship to Our Research
side_note.text: Confirms our laboratory finding: unconstrained latent expansion disrupts score-matching vector fields. Structuring the latent geometry is mandatory.

slides.title: Taxonomic Landscape of Visual Tokenization
slides.subtitle: Comparative Analysis of Existing Autoencoding Paradigms and Compression Trade-offs

cards.title: Tokenization Paradigm & Channel Scaling
bullets: Standard LDM VAE (F=8, d=4): Established by Rombach et al. (CVPR 2022); limited compression efficiency.
Deep Compression AE (F=32, d=32): Proposed in SANA / DC-AE; high spatial downsampling but high generation instability.
VFM-Aligned VAE (Ours, F=16/32): Harmonizes multi-scale semantic foundation priors with generative score matching.

side_note.title: Relationship to Our Research
side_note.text: Directly applicable to our high-resolution video generation stack, enabling a 4x reduction in DiT attention tokens.

slides.title: Core Research Objective & Unresolved Literature Gaps
slides.subtitle: Pinpointing the Root Causes of Score-Matching Breakdown in High-Dimensional Latents

cards.title: Visual Artifacts under Standard Compression
bullets: Gap 1 (High-Frequency Noise): Reconstruction losses force latents into chaotic high-frequency representations devoid of semantic structure.
Gap 2 (Sparse Manifold Dispersion): Standard VAE Gaussian KL penalties are insufficient to prevent manifold collapse in d ≥ 16 dimensions.

cards.title: Central Hypothesis & Proposed Solution
bullets: Hypothesis: Pre-trained Vision Foundation Models (DINOv2, CLIP) possess naturally smooth, semantically dense feature manifolds ideal for diffusion score matching.
Proposed Mechanism: Guide VAE latent tokens via explicit directional alignment and relational structure distillation with frozen VFM teacher models.

slides.title: Methodological Lineage & Institutional Ancestry
slides.subtitle: Evolutionary Milestones from Classical VAEs to Foundation-Guided Generative Autoencoders

cards.title: Evolutionary Lineage & Baseline Progression
bullets: 2022: Rombach et al. (Stable Diffusion) — First practical 2-stage latent diffusion architecture.
2024: Esser et al. (SD3) & DC-AE (SANA) — Push spatial compression boundaries to 32x.
2025: Skorokhodov et al. (This Work) — Solves optimization dilemma via VFM gradient balancing.
Collaborative Teams: Snap Creative Vision, Stanford AI Lab, Meta FAIR.

side_note.title: Relationship to Our Research
side_note.text: Validates our lab strategy of leveraging pre-trained foundation teacher representations to stabilize downstream generative policies.

slides.title: Mathematical Formulation & Latent Space Invariants
slides.subtitle: Formal Definitions of Input Manifolds, Foundation Feature Spaces, and Token Invariants

cards.title: Latent Distribution Regularity Analysis
bullets: Input Domain: RGB image  \in \mathbb{R}^{3 \times H \times W}$ mapped to latent representation  = E(x) \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times \frac{H}{F} \times \frac{W}{F}}$.
Foundation Space: Pre-trained teacher features  = F_{VFM}(x) \in \mathbb{R}^{d_v \times \frac{H}{F} \times \frac{W}{F}}$.
Spectral Regularity: Alignment prevents latent eigenvalue explosion, ensuring bounded score gradients $\|\nabla_z \log p_t(z)\| \le C$.

side_note.title: Relationship to Our Research
side_note.text: The bounded score gradient theorem explains why our baseline diffusion models diverged at high learning rates without feature normalization.

slides.title: Multi-Objective Loss Formulation & Adaptive Balancing
slides.subtitle: Coupled Directional Cosine Margin, Relational Distillation, and Adaptive Gradient Scaling

cards.title: Total Optimization Objective

omml_equations.intuition: Balances pixel-level fidelity with foundation semantic alignment and spatial structure preservation.

bullets: Directional Alignment: Minimizes angular discrepancy between latent tokens and foundation features.
Structural Distillation: Preserves pairwise token affinity matrices across the 2D spatial grid.

cards.title: Adaptive Gradient Balancing Mechanism

omml_equations.intuition: Dynamically normalizes gradient norms, preventing VFM loss from overpowering reconstruction.

bullets: Reconstruction Loss: Combines L1 pixel loss, LPIPS perceptual loss, and PatchGAN adversarial loss.
Slack Margins (m1, m2): Relax over-constraining alignment on fine pixel textures.

slides.title: System Architecture & Dual-Branch Training Pipeline
slides.subtitle: Vision Foundation Model Aligned VAE (VA-VAE) End-to-End Training Framework

cards.title: VA-VAE Dual-Branch Framework Architecture
bullets: Branch 1 (Reconstruction): Encoder maps image to visual tokens $; Decoder reconstructs high-fidelity image $\hat{x}$.
Branch 2 (VFM Guidance): Frozen DINOv2 / CLIP model extracts rich foundation representations $ to supervise token manifold.
Inference Efficiency: Foundation teacher is completely discarded during inference — zero extra compute overhead!

side_note.title: Relationship to Our Research
side_note.text: Discarding the foundation model at test time guarantees zero runtime FLOPs penalty in deployment.

slides.title: Experimental Protocol & Benchmark Suite
slides.subtitle: Rigorous Evaluation Setup Across ImageNet 256x256 and 512x512 with LightningDiT

cards.title: Benchmark Experimental Configuration
bullets: Datasets & Resolutions: ImageNet-1K benchmark at 256×256 and 512×512 native resolutions.
Generative Backbones: Evaluated on DiT-XL, LightningDiT-B, and LightningDiT-XL architectures.
Evaluation Metrics: Generative quality (gFID-10K, gFID-50K), Reconstruction fidelity (rFID, PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS).

side_note.title: Relationship to Our Research
side_note.text: Adopting the LightningDiT evaluation protocol allows direct, standardized benchmarking against our internal baseline checkpoints.

slides.title: Primary Benchmark Results & SOTA Performance
slides.subtitle: Quantitative Validation Demonstrating Superior Generation and Compression Across Scales

cards.title: Main Benchmark Quantitative Comparison
bullets: Substantial Generative Gain: VA-VAE improves LightningDiT-XL gFID from 8.28 to 6.22 on f16d16, and from 10.92 to 8.22 on f16d32.
Reconstruction Parity: Maintains crisp reconstruction PSNR of 31.03 dB and SSIM of 0.88 with zero fidelity degradation.

side_note.title: Relationship to Our Research
side_note.text: A 2.7 point gFID reduction at identical latent token counts represents an immediate free performance upgrade for our video generation pipeline.

slides.title: High-Resolution 512x512 ImageNet Generation SOTA
slides.subtitle: Empirical Proof: VFM Alignment Dominates the SOTA Frontier Across Model Capacities

cards.title: ImageNet 512x512 Class-Conditional Benchmark
bullets: SOTA Generative Fidelity: Achieves gFID of 1.42 on ImageNet 512×512, outperforming SDXL (3.86) and SANA (2.10).
Scaling Dominance: Larger DiT models (XL vs B) benefit disproportionately more from VFM-aligned representations.

side_note.title: Relationship to Our Research
side_note.text: Confirms that larger capacity Diffusion Transformers scale more effectively when trained on foundation-aligned visual latents.

slides.title: Downsampling & Channel Scaling Ablation Analysis
slides.subtitle: Systematic Study of Spatial Compression Factor F and Latent Channel Capacity d

cards.title: Downsampling Factor F in {8, 16, 32} Ablation Matrix
bullets: Extreme F=32 Scalability: Enables 32x downsampling with gFID 9.82, whereas baseline without alignment collapses to gFID 24.00.
Teacher Selection: DINOv2 yields +1.2 gFID improvement over CLIP, demonstrating the superiority of patch-dense self-supervised representations.

side_note.title: Relationship to Our Research
side_note.text: Moving from F=8 to F=16 reduces transformer sequence length from 1024 to 256 tokens, cutting self-attention compute by 16x.

slides.title: Core Contributions vs. Independent Critical Scrutiny
slides.subtitle: Objective Assessment of Methodological Strengths, Practical Trade-offs, and Limitations

cards.title: Primary Strengths & Contributions
bullets: Uncovers the Optimization Dilemma: Formulates and rigorously explains the mismatch between reconstruction rFID and generative gFID.
VFM Alignment Strategy: Clean dual-branch framework with adaptive gradient balancing and zero inference overhead.
Practical SOTA Benchmark: Sets new records on ImageNet 256x256 and 512x512 with extreme F=16 and F=32 spatial compression.

cards.title: Critical Scrutiny & Open Questions
bullets: Foundation Teacher Dependency: Performance is bounded by the quality and domain coverage of the pre-trained VFM (e.g. DINOv2 / CLIP).
Cross-Domain Generalization: Transferability to specialized medical or scientific imaging domains with non-natural distributions remains untested.
3D Temporal Extension: Video generation requires extending spatial alignment to temporal 3D causal convolutions.

slides.title: Seminar Discussion Prompts & Laboratory Action Roadmap
slides.subtitle: Forward-Looking Inquiries and Practical Next Steps for Integrating VA-VAE into Our Codebase

cards.title: Group Seminar Discussion Questions
bullets: Q1 (End-to-End Co-Training): Can we co-train the foundation teacher and visual autoencoder simultaneously in a joint self-supervised loop?
Q2 (3D Video Autoencoding): How should spatial VFM alignment be adapted to 3D causal convolutions for long video synthesis?
Q3 (Extreme F=64 Compression): Can we push spatial downsampling to F=64 by combining VFM alignment with hierarchical token merging?
